sensors.name: Orbital thrust cue
sensors.neutral: 50% guided throttle; absent on landing-only flights

trainingAlgorithm: Paired complete-graph reward search. Incumbent and both candidates share seeds and physical conditions. Maximize safe landings, then mean shaped reward. Mixed courses use four flights; single missions use three. One nominal flight per batch, remaining flights randomized at the selected level.
perturbationLineage: 46-input initialization distilled from pinned previous complete-graph pilots, then on-policy refinement. Current reward search perturbs control-head gains at 0.03 and all coefficients independently at 0.003.

initialization.method: Complete-graph policy distillation into a consistent 46-channel sensor schema
initialization.teacher: Previous complete-graph checkpoint, with explicit guidance retained

comparison.baselineSensorAdapter: Both pilots sample equivalent physical quantities with the same deterministic noise rule, encoded in their respective schemas. Closed-loop trajectories differ. Extra feedback channels have no old equivalent. Orbital guidance is unchanged.

variability.distributions: Bounded normal physical scales; deterministic bounded sensor jitter. Exact scales are recorded per flight.

feedbackInterventions.method: Replay the exact pre-decision graph state with one feedback group neutralized; report changed command minus actual command.
feedbackInterventions.limitation: One sampled decision per pilot. These tests establish command sensitivity and exact state restoration, not a whole-flight benefit or independent learning advantage.

arousalExperiment.method: Paired full-network operational experiment. Same readout weights and initial conditions; only the gain applied before each neuron activation changes. One nominal and one randomized seed per profile.
limitations: Twelve flights per gain across six profiles are a small exploratory sample.
No retraining between gain conditions. This does not test learning speed or a biological stimulant.
The global gain rule is an authored abstraction; chemical concentrations, receptors and cell-specific octopamine effects are not modeled.

sources.title: Octopamine neurons mediate flight-induced modulation of visual processing in Drosophila
Dopamine-mediated interactions between short- and long-term memory dynamics

checks: Complete graph integrity and independent neuron calculations
Original eight nominal mission dynamics unchanged
46-channel schema, deterministic variation and authoritative motion/actuator feedback
Exact full-network sensor replay and restoration
Every new feedback group affects the learned commands in sampled decisions
Baseline arousal preserves every tested neuron and command exactly; elevated-gain replay, edge intervention and checkpoint training checks pass
Presentation interpolation does not modify physics
Orbital conservation, premature-success rejection and ordered milestones
limitations: Eight held-out seeds per profile, four nominal and four varied, form a finite simulator evaluation. Every failure is included.
Changing the sensory mapping, initialization and training together prevents attributing a performance difference solely to feedback inputs.
A sampled command intervention does not establish a whole-flight benefit.
The arousal study holds weights fixed and does not measure training benefit, learning speed or biological chemical effects.
The world and vehicle are stylized; orbital distances and periods are compressed.
Orbital trajectory, attitude and thrust cues are engineered; this is not a learned orbital planner.
Readouts were initialized from demonstrations before reward training.
Individual biological synapse counts and signs stay fixed; output readout weights learn.
A simplified signed-rate model is not a validated biological fly emulation.
status: Historical V8 instrument-trained evaluation; not embodied validation and predates V9 orbital cadence/coast changes
